title: Domain-Driven Design
summary: The vocabulary of modeling complex business domains in software — bounded contexts and ubiquitous language, the eight context-map patterns, entities and value objects, aggregates and consistency boundaries, domain events, repositories, hexagonal architecture, event storming, and how DDD pairs with microservices and event sourcing.

inspiredBy.title: Domain-Driven Design (Evans) + Implementing DDD (Vernon) + DDD Distilled (Vernon)

chapters.title: Why DDD
chapters.summary: Design vs accidental architecture — the cost of modeling the wrong thing, why software design matters more as systems grow, the knowledge-crunching loop, and when DDD pays off vs when it's overkill.

chapters.title: Strategic Design
chapters.summary: The DDD high-level concepts — bounded context as the most important boundary in DDD, context map as the system-level view, ubiquitous language inside each context, and core/supporting/generic subdomain distinction.

chapters.title: Context Map Patterns
chapters.summary: Eight relationship types between bounded contexts — partnership, shared kernel, customer-supplier, conformist, anticorruption layer (ACL), open host service (OHS), published language, and the big ball of mud.

chapters.title: Tactical Patterns Overview
chapters.summary: The building blocks of domain models — entities, value objects, aggregates, domain events, services, repositories, factories; the relationship between them and the layer they live in.

chapters.title: Entities
chapters.summary: Identity over time — what makes something an entity vs a value object, identity allocation strategies (DB-generated, application-generated UUID/ULID), equality semantics, identity vs reference, and the identity-spanning-aggregates rule.

chapters.title: Value Objects
chapters.summary: Equality by value — immutability, side-effect-free behavior, replacing primitives with VOs (Money, Email, PhoneNumber), and the modeling power of small VOs vs primitive obsession.

chapters.title: Aggregates
chapters.summary: Consistency boundaries — aggregate root as the single entry point, invariant enforcement within the aggregate, transactional consistency vs eventual consistency between aggregates, designing for the right aggregate size.

chapters.title: Domain Events
chapters.summary: What happened in the domain — explicit modeling of past tense facts, event publication patterns, integration via events, and the distinction between domain events (intra-context) and integration events (cross-context).

chapters.title: Repositories
chapters.summary: Collection-like interface over persistence — repository per aggregate root, query patterns (CRUD-style vs specification pattern), repository vs DAO distinction, and the ORM-repository tension.

chapters.title: Domain Services
chapters.summary: Operations that don't belong on an entity or value object — stateless domain logic spanning multiple aggregates, the distinction from application services and infrastructure services, and the over-use anti-pattern.

chapters.title: Hexagonal Architecture
chapters.summary: Ports and adapters — separating the domain core from technology choices, primary ports (driving) vs secondary ports (driven), the onion/clean architecture variants, and the dependency rule (point inward).

chapters.title: Event Storming
chapters.summary: Alberto Brandolini's collaborative modeling workshop — orange stickies for domain events, blue for commands, yellow for aggregates; big-picture vs process-level vs design-level event storming, and how it accelerates DDD adoption.

chapters.title: DDD in 2026
chapters.summary: DDD with microservices (bounded contexts = service boundaries), DDD + event sourcing pairing, modular monoliths as a DDD-aligned alternative, ACL patterns for legacy migration, and AI-assisted domain modeling.
